subject: Private GPU pool sizing: admission policy & capacity alignment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@edgebound.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-07T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Private GPU pool: throughput & scaling questions

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start to scope the private deployment (VPC) for Edgebound, I want to confirm our requirements so procurement can size hardware and the network team can pre-provision circuits. High level asks:

- Target sustained throughput: ~200 QPS for our embedding+rerank pipeline (90% of traffic).
- Burst profile: up to 800 QPS for 60s windows during peaks.
- Latency targets: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 220ms for generation endpoints.
- Isolation: single-tenant, private subnet with no internet egress for model payloads.

Two immediate questions for you/your ops team:
1) What initial GPU commit (count/instance type) would Redwood recommend to meet the sustained + burst profile with 10–20% safety margin?
2) What admission policy and warm-pool plan would you propose so bursts hit headroom without cold-start tail latency?

Also attaching our security questionnaire link for legal to track — they may follow up. Can we aim for a quick alignment call tomorrow?

Thanks,
Samir
Head of ML Platform
Edgebound Analytics
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgebound.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-07T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throughput & scaling questions

Samir —

Appreciate the clear numbers; that helps. Short answer: we recommend an initial reserved pool sized for sustained QPS with a small warm burst layer and admission tiers. Summary recommendation (initial commit):

- Hardware: 8x A100-80GB equivalence (can be mapped to N vendor shapes) — expected sustained capacity ~220 QPS for your mixed embedding+rerank mix with our batching defaults.
- Warm pool: 2x smaller nodes reserved for fast bursts (pre-warmed KV cache) to absorb short spikes up to ~400 QPS without onboarding extra GPU capacity.
- Burst autoscale: policy to add slab units up to additional 6x nodes to reach peak ~800 QPS within 45–90s depending on warmup cadence.
- Admission policy (proposal):
  * Tier 1 (latency-critical): guaranteed lanes, token-level accounting, p95 SLO enforcement.
  * Tier 2 (best-effort): opportunistic batching; will be throttled during sustained saturation.
  * Fallback: automatic model-variant plumbing -> cheaper quantized variant and/or route to hosted Redwood fallback in cross-region (if allowed).

Operational notes:
- We’ll provision NICs with 25Gbps xconnects in the VPC and require egress budgeting from your networking team.
- Prefix/KV cache warmup is crucial: we recommend a scheduled warmup job ahead of business-critical windows and a short keepalive during idle windows.

I’ve attached a concise proposal PDF that sketches the math and cost delta (redwood_privgpu_proposal_v1.pdf).

Can we set a 30-minute alignment for tomorrow 10:00 PT? Laura / Karthik — can you join to confirm network expectations and admission rules?

—Hannah
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@edgebound.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-08T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throughput & scaling questions

Adding technical detail from infra/serving side — highlights and constraints for sizing and the admission policy Hannah proposed: 

1) Network egress & NIC sizing (hard reqs) - For your embedding+rerank mix we estimate peak egress ~11–14 Gbps per A100-equivalent under 800 QPS bursts (depending on sequence length and tokenization). We recommend at minimum:
   - Prod NICs: 25Gbps per host with 1.5x headroom (i.e., plan for 37–40Gbps effective path).
   - Topology: separate management plane + data plane subnets; avoid NATting model payloads through public internet.

2) Warm pool / cache strategy - Warm pool nodes keep KV caches alive and maintain hot token prefix for common prompts. Key points:
   - Warm pool size trades off cost vs. burst latency; our earlier "2x smaller nodes" is a practical starting point.
   - Time to absorb burst without scale-out depends on batch aggregation windows (we use dynamic windows: 10–50ms) and KV cache hit rate.

3) Autoscale cadence & admission logic - Proposal: staged autoscale (fast lane + slab adds):
   * Stage 0: warm pool absorbs <400 QPS instantly (0–5s).
   * Stage 1: add 2 slab units (30–60s) to cover up to ~550 QPS.
   * Stage 2: scale to full slab (up to +6 nodes, 45–90s) for sustained peak.

4) Safety and thermal considerations - Sustained high load requires thermal headroom and power planning. On-prem facilities must provide N+1 cooling across the rack groups we allocate.

Quick capacity math (back-of-envelope):
- Single A100-equivalent: sustained ~27–30 QPS for your pipeline (mixed embedding + rerank).
- 8x nodes => ~216–240 QPS sustained.
- Warm pool 2x smaller nodes => adds ~50–80 QPS immediate absorb.

Attachments: network_egress_budget.xlsx (has per-node egress calc + NIC recommendation).

I’ll bring a short runbook to the call describing failure modes (NIC saturation, KV cache cold start, admission backpressure).

—Karthik
Director, Infra & Serving
From: Samir Patel <samir@edgebound.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, legal@edgebound.ai
Date: 2027-04-08T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throughput & scaling questions

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few follow ups before we lock procurement: 

- Change windows / maintenance: what are your recommended maintenance windows and how does warm pool behave across upgrades?
- SLA & canary: can you provide a short canary plan and define the measurable SLA for latency and availability during rollout? We need this for our procurement and for legal to complete the questionnaire.
- Fallback: if we do not allow cross-region hosted fallback for data residency reasons, what are our in-VPC fallback options (model-variant, throttling knobs) and the customer-visible behavior?

We can take the numbers to our infra lead and legal. The team prefers a 3-week procurement timeline with delivery in 6–8 weeks if hardware orders go through next Monday.

Samir
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgebound.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-08T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool: throughput & scaling questions

Samir —

Answers inline and next steps. TL;DR: we can operate without cross-region fallback; canary + phased rollout with warm pool will keep user impact minimal. We attached a short MAP doc (mutual_action_plan_v1.docx).

- Change windows / maintenance: we suggest weekly 1‑hour maintenance windows (off-peak) for non-critical infra; major upgrades staged across rack groups. Warm pool nodes are treated as canary-first — they remain on the pre-upgrade image so we can validate behavioral delta before flipping production lanes.

- Canary & SLA: proposed canary plan:
  1) Canary (1 week): route 1–2% traffic to a canary slab inside your VPC (monitor p50/p95, error rate, KV miss rate).
  2) Gradual ramp (2 weeks): 10% -> 25% -> 50% with automated rollback triggers (error rate >1.5x baseline or p95 increase >30%).
  3) Full cutover: remaining traffic after 3 weeks if metrics stable.

Proposed SLA (start of service): 99.9% monthly uptime, latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 220ms. We’ll include an operational credit ladder in the contract for missed SLOs.

- In-VPC fallback options if hosted fallback is not allowed:
  * Model-variant routing: automatic switch to quantized variant with slightly higher p95 but lower resource usage.
  * Admission throttles: degrade Tier 2 workloads and maintain Tier 1 lane.
  * Graceful 429 surface with human-readable message and advisory to retry after jittered backoff.

Next steps:
1) We’ll update the proposal PDF with a refined NIC & thermal checklist (deliverable EOD tomorrow).
2) Legal: we’ll review the questionnaire you linked and start drafting SLO language for procurement.
3) Ops call booked: 2027-04-09 10:00 PT (calendar invite to follow).

Thanks — I’ll be online during the procurement review next week if you want to loop me in.

—Hannah
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
